sib1.intro: The Najdorf, English Attack: Black kicks the knight with the e-pawn, the kings castle on opposite wings, and the pawn storms start on both sides.
notes: e4 opens the game and frees the light-squared bishop.
c5 fights for the centre from the flank.
Nf3 develops the king's knight and prepares to open the centre.
d6 keeps the centre compact and lets the king's knight come out. The a-pawn advances a few moves later.
d4 opens the centre and offers a pawn to put a knight on the central square.
cxd4 takes the pawn on d4 and opens the c-file. That file is Black's main highway.
Nxd4 recaptures the pawn on d4. The knight sits in the centre.
Nf6 develops the king's knight and attacks the pawn on e4.
Nc3 develops the queen's knight and defends the pawn on e4.
a6 keeps a white piece off b5 and prepares expansion on the queenside.
Be3 develops the dark-squared bishop. White is building towards castling on the queenside.
e5 attacks the knight on d4 and gains space. The pawn on d6 stays back, which this line accepts.
Nb3 steps the knight off the pawn and leaves the dark-squared bishop on e3.
Be6 develops the light-squared bishop to an active square before the centre closes up.
f3 supports the pawn on e4 and prepares a kingside pawn advance.
Be7 develops the dark-squared bishop and prepares castling.
Qd2 develops the queen beside the bishop on e3 and prepares queenside castling.
O-O brings the king to g8 and the rook to f8. The king steps off the e-file.
O-O-O brings the king to c1 and the rook to d1. The kings are now on opposite sides.
Nbd7 develops the queen's knight without blocking the c-file.
g4 starts the pawn storm against the castled king.
b5 starts Black's own pawn storm on the queenside.

sib2.intro: The Dragon: the bishop fianchettoes, the kings castle on opposite wings, and Black breaks in the centre before the queen settles on the a-file.
notes: e4 opens the game and frees the light-squared bishop.
c5 fights for the centre from the flank.
Nf3 develops the king's knight and prepares to open the centre.
d6 controls e5 and lets the king's knight come out.
d4 opens the centre and offers a pawn to put a knight on the central square.
cxd4 takes the pawn on d4 and opens the c-file.
Nxd4 recaptures the pawn on d4. The knight sits in the centre.
Nf6 develops the king's knight and attacks the pawn on e4.
Nc3 develops the queen's knight and defends the pawn on e4.
g6 prepares the fianchetto. The dark-squared bishop wants the long diagonal.
Be3 develops the dark-squared bishop and defends the knight on d4.
Bg7 puts the dark-squared bishop on the long diagonal. The knight on f6 stands in front of it for now.
f3 supports the pawn on e4 and prepares a kingside advance. It also keeps the knight on f6 out of g4, where it would hit the bishop on e3.
O-O brings the king to g8 and the rook to f8. The king sits behind the fianchetto.
Qd2 develops the queen beside the bishop on e3. White is ready to castle long.
Nc6 develops the queen's knight and attacks the knight on d4.
O-O-O brings the king to c1 and the rook to d1. Opposite-side castling means both attacks will race.
d5 breaks in the centre and attacks the pawn on e4. Black challenges the centre before White's attack lands.
exd5 takes the pawn on d5 and accepts the opening of the centre.
Nxd5 recaptures the pawn on d5. The knight arrives in the centre.
Nxc6 takes the knight on c6 and damages the queenside pawns.
bxc6 recaptures the knight on c6. The b-file is half-open against White's queenside.
Bd4 offers a trade of the dark-squared bishops and attacks the bishop on g7. White wants that bishop off the long diagonal.
Bxd4 takes the bishop on d4. Black accepts the trade.
Qxd4 recaptures the bishop on d4. The queen stands in the centre.
Qb6 attacks the queen on d4 and puts pressure down the half-open b-file.
Na4 attacks the queen on b6 and steps the knight towards the queenside.
Qa5 steps the queen off the knight and keeps her on the queenside.

sib3.intro: The Richter-Rauzer: the bishop comes to g5, White castles long and plays the f-pawn, and after the trade in the centre Black's queen comes to the a-file.
notes: e4 opens the game and frees the light-squared bishop.
c5 fights for the centre from the flank.
Nf3 develops the king's knight and prepares to open the centre.
d6 controls e5 and lets the king's knight come out.
d4 opens the centre and offers a pawn to put a knight on the central square.
cxd4 takes the pawn on d4 and opens the c-file.
Nxd4 recaptures the pawn on d4. The knight sits in the centre.
Nf6 develops the king's knight and attacks the pawn on e4.
Nc3 develops the queen's knight and defends the pawn on e4.
Nc6 develops the queen's knight and attacks the knight on d4.
Bg5 develops the dark-squared bishop and attacks the knight on f6. This is the Rauzer, and the pawn on e7 still stands between that knight and the queen.
e6 reinforces the centre and frees the dark-squared bishop. The pawn leaves e7, so the bishop on g5 now pins the knight on f6 to the queen.
Qd2 develops the queen and prepares queenside castling. She also stands behind the bishop on g5.
Be7 develops the dark-squared bishop and breaks the pin on the knight on f6.
O-O-O brings the king to c1 and the rook to d1. The rook looks up the half-open d-file.
O-O brings the king to g8 and the rook to f8. The king steps off the e-file.
f4 gains space and prepares to open the f-file. The Rauzer attack is under way.
Nxd4 takes the knight on d4 and draws the queen to the centre.
Qxd4 recaptures the knight on d4. The queen takes a central post.
Qa5 attacks the knight on c3 and develops the queen.
Kb1 steps the king off the c-file. Black's c-file is already half open.
Rd8 puts the rook on the d-file, behind the pawn on d6.

sib4.intro: The Sveshnikov: Black plays the e-pawn, one white knight goes to a3, the other lands on d5, and Black's dark-squared bishop takes back on f6 and becomes active.
notes: e4 opens the game and frees the light-squared bishop.
c5 fights for the centre from the flank.
Nf3 develops the king's knight and prepares to open the centre.
Nc6 develops the queen's knight and fights for the central squares.
d4 opens the centre and offers a pawn to put a knight on the central square.
cxd4 takes the pawn on d4 and opens the c-file.
Nxd4 recaptures the pawn on d4. The knight sits in the centre.
Nf6 develops the king's knight and attacks the pawn on e4.
Nc3 develops the queen's knight and defends the pawn on e4.
e5 attacks the knight on d4 and gains space. Black accepts a hole in the centre for that space.
Ndb5 jumps deep into Black's position. That knight has to be met.
d6 supports the pawn on e5 and occupies the square the knight was attacking.
Bg5 pins the knight on f6 to the queen on d8.
a6 asks the knight a question and begins the queenside advance.
Na3 steps the knight to the edge. The other knight is the one headed for the central hole.
b5 gains queenside space and takes away the knight's natural route back.
Nd5 plants the queen's knight on the central hole and attacks the knight on f6.
Be7 develops the dark-squared bishop and breaks the pin on the knight on f6.
Bxf6 takes the knight on f6. White removes a defender of the dark squares.
Bxf6 recaptures the bishop on f6. The dark-squared bishop takes up an active post.
c3 controls d4 and gives White a solid pawn front.
Bg5 puts the dark-squared bishop on an active diagonal. White has already given up the bishop that could challenge it.

sib5.intro: A sharp open Sicilian: White pushes the e-pawn, the bishop checks from b4, and the king steps to e2 before Black hits the knight with the f-pawn.
notes: e4 opens the game and frees the light-squared bishop.
c5 fights for the centre from the flank.
Nf3 develops the king's knight and prepares to open the centre.
e6 supports a central pawn and frees the dark-squared bishop. Black keeps the position flexible.
d4 opens the centre and offers a pawn to put a knight on the central square.
cxd4 takes the pawn on d4 and opens the c-file.
Nxd4 recaptures the pawn on d4. The knight sits in the centre.
Nf6 develops the king's knight and attacks the pawn on e4.
Nc3 develops the queen's knight and defends the pawn on e4.
Nc6 develops the queen's knight and attacks the knight on d4.
Nxc6 takes the knight on c6. White removes the piece that was attacking the central knight.
bxc6 recaptures the knight on c6. A single pawn stands on the c-file, and the b-file is half-open.
e5 attacks the knight on f6 and gains space. The centre becomes a wedge.
Nd5 steps the knight off the pawn and into the centre.
Ne4 brings the queen's knight into the centre.
Qc7 develops the queen and attacks the pawn on e5.
f4 supports the pawn on e5 and gains more space.
Qb6 attacks the pawn on b2 and steps the queen onto an active diagonal.
c4 attacks the knight on d5 and gains space.
Bb4+ develops the dark-squared bishop and gives check. The knight has left c3, so the diagonal to the king is clear.
Ke2 steps the king out of check. The king cannot go to f2, because the queen on b6 covers it, and every block loses material.
f5 attacks the knight on e4 and challenges the pawn wedge.

sib6.intro: The Alapin: White plays the c-pawn and meets a pawn to d5, the queen takes back, and a knight jump sends her home.
notes: e4 opens the game and frees the light-squared bishop.
c5 fights for the centre from the flank.
c3 keeps a pawn on the c-file and prepares to meet a central break.
d5 attacks the pawn on e4 at once. Black does not let White build in peace.
exd5 takes the pawn on d5 and opens the e-file.
Qxd5 recaptures the pawn on d5. The queen comes out early, which White will try to punish.
d4 claims the centre and attacks the pawn on c5. The queen on d5 is now a target for development.
Nf6 develops the king's knight beside the queen on d5. White will use development to chase that queen.
Nf3 develops the king's knight and prepares castling. The queen on d5 is the piece this line chases.
e6 supports the centre and frees the dark-squared bishop. The queen needs a retreat.
Bd3 develops the light-squared bishop and aims at the kingside.
cxd4 takes the pawn on d4 and opens the c-file.
cxd4 recaptures the pawn on d4. White has a pawn in the centre and an open c-file to watch.
Nc6 develops the queen's knight and attacks the pawn on d4.
O-O brings the king to g1 and the rook to f1. The king steps off the e-file.
Be7 develops the dark-squared bishop and prepares castling.
Nc3 develops the queen's knight and attacks the queen on d5.
Qd6 steps the queen off the knight and stays active.
Nb5 attacks the queen on d6. The early queen is chased again.
Qd8 sends the queen home. She has spent several moves and is back where she started.

sib7.intro: The Smith-Morra Gambit: White offers a pawn for development, the bishop comes to c4, and a rook lands on the half-open d-file.
notes: e4 opens the game and frees the light-squared bishop.
c5 fights for the centre from the flank.
d4 offers a pawn to open lines and attacks the pawn on c5.
cxd4 takes the pawn on d4. Black accepts the first pawn.
c3 offers a second pawn so that a knight can recapture with tempo.
dxc3 takes the pawn on c3. Black is now a pawn up, and White must show compensation.
Nxc3 recaptures the pawn on c3 and develops the queen's knight. The gambit pawn has bought this piece.
Nc6 develops the queen's knight and fights for the centre.
Nf3 develops the king's knight. White gets a minor piece out before Black builds a pawn centre.
d6 controls e5 and frees the light-squared bishop.
Bc4 aims the light-squared bishop at the pawn on f7. The gambit wants fast piece play.
e6 blunts that bishop and frees the dark-squared bishop.
O-O brings the king to g1 and the rook to f1. The king steps off the e-file.
Nf6 develops the king's knight and attacks the pawn on e4.
Qe2 develops the queen and defends the pawn on e4.
a6 keeps White's knight and bishop off b5 and prepares queenside room.
Rd1 puts the rook on the half-open d-file, facing the pawn on d6.
Qc7 develops the queen and looks along the open c-file.
Bf4 develops the dark-squared bishop and attacks the pawn on d6.
Be7 develops the dark-squared bishop and prepares castling.

sib8.intro: The Grand Prix Attack: White plays the f-pawn and a bishop to b5, Black trades that bishop, and the centre opens.
notes: e4 opens the game and frees the light-squared bishop.
c5 fights for the centre from the flank.
Nc3 develops the queen's knight and keeps the centre flexible. White is not opening with the d-pawn yet.
Nc6 develops the queen's knight and fights for the centre.
f4 gains kingside space and prepares an attack on that wing.
g6 prepares a fianchetto against that pawn advance.
Nf3 develops the king's knight. White gets a minor piece out before Black builds a pawn centre.
Bg7 puts the dark-squared bishop on the long diagonal.
Bb5 attacks the knight on c6. The pawn on d7 still stands between that knight and the king, so this is pressure, not yet a full pin.
Nd4 is the standard jump. The knight attacks the bishop on b5 and the knight on f3.
O-O brings the king to g1 and the rook to f1. White castles before resolving the bishop.
Nxb5 takes the bishop on b5. Black removes the piece that was attacking the knight.
Nxb5 recaptures the knight on b5. The queen's knight takes up the bishop's square.
d5 attacks the pawn on e4 and opens the centre.
exd5 takes the pawn on d5 and opens the centre.
a6 asks the knight on b5 a question.
Nc3 steps the knight back to a natural square and defends the centre.
Nf6 develops the king's knight and attacks the pawn on d5.
d4 claims the centre beside the pawn on d5.
Nxd5 takes the pawn on d5 and plants the knight in the centre.

sib9.intro: The Rossolimo: the bishop takes on c6, Black takes back towards the centre, and both sides fix the queenside.
notes: e4 opens the game and frees the light-squared bishop.
c5 fights for the centre from the flank.
Nf3 develops the king's knight. White gets a minor piece out before Black builds a pawn centre.
Nc6 develops the queen's knight and fights for the centre.
Bb5 attacks the knight on c6 and offers to damage Black's queenside pawns.
g6 prepares the fianchetto rather than kicking the bishop at once.
O-O brings the king to g1 and the rook to f1. The king steps off the e-file.
Bg7 puts the dark-squared bishop on the long diagonal.
Re1 puts the rook behind the pawn on e4.
e5 takes space in the centre and frees the dark-squared bishop.
Bxc6 takes the knight on c6. White gives up the bishop to double the pawns.
dxc6 recaptures the bishop on c6 towards the centre. The c-pawns are doubled, and the light-squared bishop is free.
d3 supports the pawn on e4 and frees the dark-squared bishop.
Ne7 develops the king's knight towards the centre. The doubled pawns mean this knight does not belong on c6.
Be3 develops the dark-squared bishop and attacks the pawn on c5.
b6 prepares to develop the light-squared bishop and supports the pawn on c5.
Nbd2 develops the queen's knight without blocking the c-pawn.
O-O brings the king to g8 and the rook to f8. The king steps off the e-file.
a4 gains queenside space and restrains a pawn advance there.
a5 stops that pawn and fixes the queenside structure.

sib10.intro: The Closed Sicilian: both sides fianchetto, a knight jumps into the centre, and Black breaks with a pawn to d5 before White untangles.
notes: e4 opens the game and frees the light-squared bishop.
c5 fights for the centre from the flank.
Nc3 develops the queen's knight. White is keeping the centre closed.
Nc6 develops the queen's knight and fights for the centre.
g3 prepares the fianchetto. The light-squared bishop will sit on the long diagonal.
g6 prepares Black's own fianchetto.
Bg2 puts the light-squared bishop on the long diagonal.
Bg7 puts the dark-squared bishop on the long diagonal.
d3 supports the pawn on e4 and keeps the centre closed.
d6 supports a later central strike and mirrors White's pawn.
Be3 develops the dark-squared bishop and attacks the pawn on c5.
e6 holds the centre and keeps the long diagonal open for the bishop on g7.
Qd2 develops the queen beside the bishop on e3.
Nge7 develops the king's knight without blocking the bishop on g7.
Nge2 develops the king's knight and keeps the long diagonal open for the bishop on g2.
Nd4 plants the queen's knight on a strong central square and attacks the knight on e2.
O-O brings the king to g1 and the rook to f1. The king steps off the e-file.
O-O brings the king to g8 and the rook to f8. The king steps off the e-file.
Nd1 steps the queen's knight home and unblocks the c-pawn, which can then challenge the knight on d4.
d5 attacks the pawn on e4. Black opens the centre while the knight on d1 is still rerouting.
